package_info.package_versions: affected versions served via hijacked S3 bucket (exact versions not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The package delivered binaries from a hijacked S3 bucket, which were replaced with malicious versions that steal user credentials and system information, exfiltrating them to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

execution_context.trigger: build-time (when binary is downloaded and executed as part of npm install or package usage)
execution_context.file_location: downloaded binary from hijacked S3 bucket, executed by npm postinstall script or during package usage

malicious_snippets.code_language: binary (likely C/C++ or Node.js native addon, but actual code not shown in report)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time or postinstall, the binary collects user credentials and system information, then exfiltrates this data to the attacker's hijacked S3 bucket.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The binary, instead of performing its expected mathematical operations, collects sensitive data and sends it to an external, attacker-controlled location.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate bignum binary should only perform mathematical computations, not access credentials or exfiltrate data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate binaries may collect telemetry or crash reports, but never credentials or sensitive system info without user consent.
key_indicators: Binary replaced in S3 bucket without package maintainer's consent
Unexpected network communication to S3 bucket
Access to credentials and system information

attack_chain.action: Attacker hijacks abandoned S3 bucket used by the npm package to serve binaries.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious binaries are now served to users installing the package.

attack_chain.action: User installs or builds the npm package, triggering download and execution of the malicious binary.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious binary executes on user system.

attack_chain.action: Malicious binary collects credentials and system information.
Collected data is exfiltrated to the attacker's hijacked S3 bucket.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive user data.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network requests to S3 buckets during npm install or build
Binaries downloaded from third-party or abandoned cloud storage
Execution of binaries with credential or system info access
file_indicators: Binaries downloaded from S3 buckets not controlled by the package maintainer
Presence of postinstall scripts that fetch and execute remote binaries
network_indicators: Outbound connections to hijacked or suspicious S3 buckets
Data uploads to cloud storage not associated with the legitimate project
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that download and execute binaries from cloud storage, especially S3 buckets. Flag binaries that access credentials or system information and make outbound network connections during installation or build. Correlate package metadata with cloud storage ownership to detect abandoned or hijacked buckets.
